04/04/2020

Dr Malcolm Still
Rheumatologist
5 Grant Street
Fairmont

Dear Dr Still,
Re: Mr James Seymour                DOB: 19/09/1953

Thank you for seeing Mr Seymour, a 60-year-old man who has gout. Your further evaluation and management would be greatly appreciated.

Mr Seymour is a heavy alcohol drinker, and he has a positive family history of rheumatoid arthritis related to his father. He has been having had multiple attacks of gout since 2010, for which he is on colchicine, indomethacine and allopurinol.

On 25/04/2014, Mr Seymour presented to me with a four-weeks history of gout episode. He reported that he had been taking cholchicine and indomethacine irregularly, and he had stopped discontinued / ceased allopurinol tow two months previously. He was reluctant to take his medication because he was not satisfied with his diagnosis. On examination, his first left toe was inflamed without involvement of the other joints. Therefore, he was advised to reduce alcohol consumption and to do diet modification. The doses of indomthacine and colchicines were adjusted .in addition to, prescription of / addition of paracetamol, four mg three times a day; and oxycodone, five mg at bed time if required.

A review one week later today showed subsiding in of the attack. However, he mentioned that he had had mild diarrhea and oxycodone had been required three times only. At that time, His urate was is 0.48 m.mol/L and CRP was is 6mg/L. Consequently, allopurinol was has been re-commenced again. A ,and the possibility of synovial fluid test was has been discussed.

Based on these finding and up-on upon Mr Seymour`s insistence to rule out rheumatoid arthritis, I am referring Mr Seymour for further examination and treatment (I think treatment is not required “the gout medication is already working well!”).  (may replace with “advice”).
For any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
